source_title: North Korea's Kim calls for rapid expansion of drone technology, observes testing of weapons
source_excerpt: Seoul North Korean leader Kim Jong Un called for rapidly expanding the country's drone technology and observed tests of various weapons, state media reported Friday (October 30, 2026), as his nation remains embroiled in a standoff with rival South Korea along their heavily fortified border. https://www.thehindu.com/opinion/op-ed/reading-kim-jong-uns-mind/article62112799.ece Acquiring advanced drones is a top priority for Mr. Kim, who now wants to beef up both conventional and nuclear capabilities. Experts say his troops dispatched to Russia to support its war against Ukraine have likely gained valuable expertise in drone warfare from Russian forces and related battlefield experiences. North Korea's Kim Jong Un vows ‘exponential’ increase in nuclear forces North Korea's Kim Jong Un vows ‘exponential’ increase in nuclear forces North Korea has conducted eight missile tests, in 2026, which may reflect its efforts to take advantage of eroding international norms to cement its nuclear status North Korea's Kim Jong Un vows ‘exponential’ increase in nuclear forces storyline 1 The North’s official Korean Central News Agency said that Mr. Kim on Thursday (October 29) visited an exhibition of a variety of attack and other drones that show recent achievements in the field of unmanned aeronautical technology. In a speech at the exhibition, Mr. Kim stressed the need to seize “the absolute superiority in the drone technology” and announced unspecified steps needed to “rapidly expand and strengthen the unmanned aeronautical technology,” KCNA said. To mark the event, KCNA said that North Korea later conducted test launches of various drones, missiles and weapons from the 600 mm-calibre ultra-precision multiple rocket launchers. KCNA photos showed Mr. Kim watching soaring weapons or him clenching his fist while his teenage daughter was clapping her hands beside him. South Korea's spy agency assesses that the girl, reportedly about 13, is likely Mr. Kim's heir. North Korea warns U.S. over Taiwan while Kim pledges support for Russia North Korea warns U.S. over Taiwan while Kim pledges support for Russia North Korean leader Kim Jong Un pledged continued support for Russia and its war effort ‌in a birthday message to President Vladimir Putin North Korea warns U.S. over Taiwan while Kim pledges support for Russia storyline 1 South Korea's military earlier said it detected the launches of about 10 short-range ballistic missiles from North Korea's eastern coastal town of Wonsan on Thursday (October 29). They were North Korea's first ballistic weapons firings in 17 days. Tensions between the two Koreas have been running high since last month's land mine blasts at their border that wounded three South Korean soldiers. Seoul accused North Korea of burying the mines south of the military demarcation line and demanded an apology. But Pyongyang has denied responsibility for the explosions and warned of retaliation if provoked. Last week, North Korea threatened to resume propaganda loudspeaker broadcasts and place new weapons systems along the border. North Korea has pulled out of talks with the U.S. and South Korea after Mr. Kim's high-stakes diplomacy with U.S. President Donald Trump collapsed in 2019. In recent weeks, North Korea has dialled up weapons testing activities in a likely attempt to boost its leverage in potential diplomacy with the U.S. after Trump expressed his eagerness to restore talks with Mr. Kim. Mr. Kim has recently taken steps to cement ties with China, North Korea's economic pipeline, after years of prioritising ties with Russia, including by supplying thousands of troops and ammunition, likely in return for economic and military assistance. Meanwhile, Switzerland's Foreign Minister Ignazio Cassis arrived in North Korea on Thursday (October 29) to see the reopening of Switzerland's diplomatic office in Pyongyang and meet North Korean officials. He is travelling on to South Korea on Friday (October 20).
